To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) mirror neurons are a special class of visuo-motor neurons, (2) mirror neurons are active when the monkey observes a goal-oriented action, (3) the activity of mirror neurons is selective for the type of action observed and for its goal, and (4) mirror neurons are also active when the monkey performs the same action.
